key_insight: Lead-free AgBiS2 memristors can achieve ultra-low-voltage, high-ratio switching with controllable filament evolution from digital to analog modes for neuromorphic functions.
engineering_relevance: Thickness and interface engineering provide a practical route to tune switching behavior and improve reliability in sustainable, solution-processable memory devices.
method: Used solution-processed AgBiS2 memristor devices with interface and thickness engineering.
Applied first-principles calculations to identify native defects and ionic migration barriers.
Combined electrochemical impedance, pulse tests, and post-operando structural analysis to link transport and morphology to switching.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an ultra-low SET voltage of about 0.08 V, an ON/OFF ratio greater than 10^4, and gradual conductance modulation under pulse trains.
watch_item: Repeated filament formation and rupture can drive substantial structural evolution, which may affect endurance and variability over long-term operation.
paper_title: Controlling Switching Evolution in Lead-Free Perovskite-Inspired Chalcogenide Memristors for Neuromorphic Computing
